description: bf16 baseline disambiguation for the two 2026 flagship models that produced negative ΔPPL under method (B) asymmetric per-channel INT3 without norm separation in Phase 19. Tests whether the anomaly is an FP16 inference artifact (H1) or a real regularization effect (H2).

H1.label: FP16 eval artifact
H1.statement: Both models are bf16-trained. FP16 inference adds numerical instability that quantization noise partially masks, producing an apparent improvement vs inflated FP16 baseline. A bf16 baseline should eliminate the negative ΔPPL.
H1.decision_rule: supported if bf16 baseline drops by > 0.1 AND asym-only ΔPPL shrinks toward zero / flips positive under bf16

H2.label: Real regularization effect
H2.statement: Quantization noise is genuinely acting as beneficial regularization on well-trained 2026 models. A bf16 baseline should preserve the negative ΔPPL.
H2.decision_rule: supported if bf16 baseline is stable (within 0.05) AND asym-only ΔPPL stays negative under bf16

Qwen3.5-9B/fp16.label: Qwen3.5-9B
Qwen3.5-9B/fp16.silent_force_note: Qwen3.5-9B is trained natively in bf16 and the transformers library silently upcasts the requested torch_dtype=float16 back to bf16 on load. The 'fp16' run therefore never actually evaluated in FP16. The fp16-vs-bf16 comparison for Qwen3.5 is degenerate; both rows below are genuine bf16 measurements.

Qwen3.5-9B/bf16.label: Qwen3.5-9B
Qwen3.5-9B/bf16.interpretation: All numbers match the 'fp16' row bit-for-bit because transformers silently forced bf16 there too. The -0.0038 B-delta persists at native bf16 -- it is not an FP16 artifact. It is also within the plausible measurement-noise floor (~0.05 PPL at 5120 prediction tokens), so Qwen3.5 is best read as 'no detectable anomaly on this metric'.

Qwen3.5-9B.comparison_valid_note: Both 'fp16' and 'bf16' runs executed in bf16 due to library-forced upcast. Cannot disambiguate H1 vs H2 for this model on dtype alone.
Qwen3.5-9B.verdict_under_script_rule: H2_supported (by the decision rule: stable baseline + B stays negative)
Qwen3.5-9B.verdict_honest: inconclusive; the -0.0038 B-delta is within measurement noise on 5120 prediction tokens

gemma-4-E4B.verdict_honest: H1 ruled out with high confidence. Baseline shift (0.019) is well inside measurement noise; B-delta remains strongly negative at -0.32 even under native bf16. The 27% shrinkage hints some FP16-specific effect contributes at the margin but cannot be the primary driver. H2 is the best-fitting explanation among the two pre-registered hypotheses.

findings.F1_H1_ruled_out: FP16 eval artifact (H1) is not the explanation for the negative B-ΔPPL on gemma-4-E4B. Baseline shift under native bf16 is only 0.019 (well below the 0.1 H1 threshold), and B-delta remains strongly negative at -0.32.
findings.F2_Qwen35_inconclusive: Qwen3.5-9B cannot be cleanly disambiguated by dtype alone because the library forces bf16 on load. Its -0.004 B-delta is within measurement noise in either reading.
findings.F3_real_mechanism_open: The genuine negative ΔPPL on gemma-4-E4B under (B) asym-only is mechanistically unexplained by our pre-registered hypotheses. Three post-hoc candidates: (H3) the raw-x per-channel min/max window acts as a token-level clipping filter that incidentally cleans up some Gemma 4 attention state; (H4) gemma-4-E4B is multimodal-trained, and feeding text-only leaves the model over-confident, so quantization noise raises entropy back toward the trained distribution; (H5) partial contamination of WikiText-2 in pre-training. None of these is tested here; flagged as open for future work.
findings.F4_D_is_robust: The v0.3 recommended recipe (D) = nsep+pchan asym produces ordinary small-positive ΔPPL on both models (+0.09 Qwen3.5, +0.93-1.16 Gemma 4). The negative-ΔPPL anomaly is confined to the (B) ablation variant, not to the method we ship.

verdict_overall: H2 supported for gemma-4-E4B; Qwen3.5-9B inconclusive due to forced-bf16 library behavior. The core v0.3 claim in Phase 17 (8-model generalization, all in production tier under D) is UNAFFECTED -- D does not exhibit negative ΔPPL, only the B ablation does, and only on gemma-4-E4B.
